custom_logic_notes: ColorAML is a custom indicator with buffer1 acting as a color/trend state: 0=downtrend (sell signal), 2=uptrend (buy signal). Entry only triggers on transition: BUY_Open requires Value[1]==2 AND Value[0]!=2 (color changed to uptrend). SELL_Open requires Value[1]==0 AND Value[0]!=0 (color changed to downtrend). SignalBar=1 means signals are read from the previous completed bar (bar index 1), reducing repainting risk. CIsNewBar class from TradeAlgorithms.mqh handles new bar detection. LoadHistory() ensures history data is available. GlobalVariableDel_() cleans up on deinit. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library provides all trade execution wrappers (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose) with signal time tracking to prevent duplicate entries.
python_conversion_notes: Two main components need manual implementation: (1) ColorAML indicator - must obtain or reverse-engineer the AML (Adaptive Moving Level) algorithm from its .mq5 source. The indicator uses Fractal=6 and Lag=7 parameters. Buffer 1 outputs a discrete color state (0=down, 1=neutral, 2=up). (2) TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions - these are standard trade wrappers that can be replaced with simple market order execution in Python. The position sizing logic is straightforward: negative MM = fixed lots, positive MM = deposit fraction. The new-bar guard and signal-on-transition logic are easy to replicate. Key conversion: ColorAML buffer1 values 0/2 as trend state with transition detection for entry signals.
